title: GPU Reserve Commander — micro-dash and scaling threshold editor
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Design a compact, single-pane control and status surface for Dedicated GPU pools that surfaces per-pool health, cost impact, autoscale thresholds, and a burst-credit editor. The micro-dash is intended for on-call and SRE workflows: quick triage, immediate throttle/cooldown actions, and safe scaling edits without navigating into deep settings. Deliverables: high-fidelity prototype, annotated interaction spec, accessibility checklist, and handoff package for frontend and product engineering.
decisions: Single-row micro-dash: condensed health, latency sparkline, burst-credit meter, and primary action. Rationale: rapid skim by on-call engineers without context switching.

Allow inline threshold edits with a safety preview and an explicit Apply button rather than live changes. Rationale: avoid accidental autoscale policy drift; frontend will call a 'preview' API before commit.
Use color and icon redundancy for health states (green/yellow/red + filled/pulse icons) to increase scanning reliability and WCAG contrast.
Expose cost delta per 1k tokens as a micro-metric on hover for autoscale policy changes to make trade-offs visible in situ.
Burst credits modeled as discrete buckets with decrement animation; chosen over continuous slider because credit rounding matches backend accounting and reduces accidental overcommit.
Include a one-click rollback to last autoscale profile for the pool; backend will persist last-config with a 7-day retention window.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype demonstrates key flows: triage (identify hot pool), emergency throttle (reduce burst to 0), adjust scale thresholds (+/- CPU/latency target), preview cost impact, and apply changes.
Design tokens and spacing follow Console design system; components are tokenized and annotated for frontend devs.
Accessibility report completed: keyboard nav, screen-reader labels for burst meter and threshold editor, high-contrast modes validated.
Handoff includes interaction spec and list of required backend flags/APIs: autoscale-preview, burst-adjust, rollback-to-last.
Usability test: 6 participants (SREs/Platform Engineers) with success rate >= 83% for emergency throttle and threshold edit tasks.
